extracted.intended_audience: Entities and individuals applying for FCC authorizations and participating in FCC competitive bidding (auction) proceedings; compliance officers and legal counsel for bidders; FCC staff administering auctions and debt collection
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing FCC auctions and related applicant qualifications, plus adjacent Commission policies on debt collection, reporting, interagency coordination, and anti-drug certifications that affect eligibility. Includes bidding design options, auction mechanisms, payment/penalty rules, short-form application requirements, and definitions of control for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and accrual of interest/charges on debts (31 U.S.C. 3717)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will mail, hand-deliver, or use other forms of transmission, including facsimile telecopier service, a written notice to the debtor, at the debtor's CORES contact address explaining the Commission's requirements concerning these charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges (interest, penalties, administrative costs) shall continue to accrue until the debt is paid in full or otherwise resolved through compromise, termination, or waiver. This provision does not modify contract terms or the Commission's rights under its rules regarding notice or waiver of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest accrual date
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest shall accrue from the date of delinquency, or as otherwise provided by the terms of any contract, note, or security agreement, regulation, or law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest rate determination (Treasury rate and higher-rate exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise established in a contract, note, or security agreement, repayment agreement, or by statute, the rate of interest charged shall be the rate established annually by the Treasury in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3717.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3717, an agency may charge a higher rate of interest if it reasonably determines that a higher rate is necessary to protect the rights of the United States; the agency should document the reason(s) for that determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed initial interest rate and treatment on default
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate of interest, as initially charged, shall remain fixed for the duration of the indebtedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a debtor defaults and seeks a new repayment agreement, the agency may require interest at a new rate reflecting the current value of funds to the Treasury at the time the new agreement is executed. Interest shall not be compounded (no interest on interest, penalties, or administrative costs). Charges that accrued but were not collected under a defaulted agreement may be added to the principal under a new repayment agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall assess administrative costs incurred for processing and handling delinquent debts, unless otherwise prohibited by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation may be based on actual costs incurred or upon estimated costs as determined by the Commission. Administrative costs include personnel and service costs (e.g., telephone, copier, overhead) to notify and collect the debt, without regard to the success of collection efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty on delinquent debt (up to 6% per year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise established in a contract, repayment agreement, or by statute, the Commission will charge a penalty, pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3717(e)(2), currently not to exceed six percent (6%) a year on the amount due on a debt that is delinquent for more than 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This charge shall accrue from the date of delinquency. If the statutory rate changes, the Commission will apply that rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-of-living adjustment as alternative to interest/penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may increase an administrative debt by the cost of living adjustment in lieu of charging interest and penalties under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative debt includes fines, penalties, overpayments, but not debts based on extension of Government credit (loans). COLA is computed annually using the June Consumer Price Index comparison. Agencies should use this alternative only when there is a legitimate reason (e.g., calculating interest/penalties would be extremely difficult due to age of the debt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of application of partial/instalment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a debt is paid in partial or installment payments, amounts received shall be applied first to outstanding penalties and administrative cost charges, second to accrued interest, and third to the outstanding principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of charges for payments within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will waive the collection of interest and administrative charges imposed pursuant to this section on the portion of the debt that is paid within 30 days after the date on which interest began to accrue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day period will not be extended except for good cause shown of extraordinary and compelling circumstances, completely documented and submitted before the expiration of the first 30-day period. The Commission may waive interest, penalties, and administrative costs in whole or part on good cause shown, either under compromise criteria or if collection is against equity and good conscience or not in the best interest of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common law authority for interest on non-31 U.S.C. 3717 debts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission retains the common law right to impose interest and related charges on debts not subject to 31 U.S.C. 3717.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from Debt Collection Act remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Debt Collection Act remedies/procedures (administrative offset, use of credit bureaus, contracting for collection agencies, interest and related charges) do not apply to debts arising under or payments made under the Internal Revenue Code, the Social Security Act (except as provided), or tariff laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These remedies may still be authorized for otherwise-exempt debts if authorized under some other statute or common law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency collection authority for employees and other debts
rubrics_metrics.description: This section should not be construed as prohibiting use of these authorities when collecting debts owed by persons employed by agencies administering the cited laws unless the debt arose under those laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission is authorized to assess interest and related charges on debts not subject to 31 U.S.C. 3717 to the extent authorized under common law or other statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusivity of remedies and other sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedies and sanctions available in this subpart are not exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may impose other sanctions, where permitted by law, for any inexcusable, prolonged, or repeated failure to pay such a claim; notice to the debtor will be provided as required by law prior to imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting discharged debts to the Internal Revenue Service (Form 1099-C)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission discharges a debt for less than the full value of indebtedness, it will report the outstanding balance discharged, not including interest, to the IRS using Form 1099-C when: (1) principal amount not in dispute is $600 or more; (2) obligation not discharged in bankruptcy; and (3) obligation is no longer collectible because statute expired during the tax year or a formal compromise agreement was reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Treasury will prepare Form 1099-C for debts transferred to Treasury for collection and deemed uncollectible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative offset against tax refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will take action to effect administrative offset against tax refunds due to debtors under 26 U.S.C. 6402, in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3720A and Treasury Department regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and disclosure of mailing addresses obtained from IRS
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may request a debtor's mailing address from the IRS to locate a debtor and is authorized to use mailing addresses obtained to enforce collection and may disclose such addresses to other agencies and to collection agencies for collection purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency requests for administrative or salary offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to the Commission by other Federal agencies for administrative or salary offset shall be in writing and forwarded to the Financial Operations Center; requests by the Commission to other agencies shall be in writing and forwarded certified return receipt as specified by that agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests shall be accompanied by a certification that the debtor owes the debt (including amount) and that the procedures for administrative or salary offset have been fully complied with. Requests shall be processed within 30 calendar days or notice to extend for another 30 days shall be forwarded 10 days prior to expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose re Anti-Drug Abuse Act (eligibility determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine eligibility for professional and/or commercial licenses issued by the Commission with respect to any denials of Federal benefits imposed by Federal and/or state courts under authority granted in 21 U.S.C. 862.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5301 certification requirement for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants for new, modified, or renewed instruments of authorization must certify that neither the applicant nor any party to the application is subject to a denial of Federal benefits that includes FCC benefits pursuant to section 5301 of the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1988 (21 U.S.C. 862).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the certification is on the FCC application form, no separate certification is needed. If not on form, applicant must attach certification to written application. An applicant unable to certify is ineligible and has 90 days from filing to comply. Failure to respond to the certification question on a form will result in dismissal under relevant processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'party to the application' for section 5301 purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to the application includes: (1) if applicant is an individual, that individual; (2) if corporation or unincorporated association, all officers, directors, or persons holding 5% or more of outstanding stock; (3) if partnership, all non-limited partners and any limited partners holding 5% or more interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from section 5301 certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The section 5301 certification provisions are not applicable to the Amateur Radio Service, Citizens Band Radio Service, Radio Control Radio Service, users in Public Mobile Services and Private Radio Services that are not individually licensed, or to Federal, State or local governmental entities or subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive bidding eligibility — mutual exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutually exclusive initial applications are subject to competitive bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain types of license applications are not subject to competitive bidding (see next criterion). Specific service rules should also be consulted to determine applicable bidding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to competitive bidding (non-auctionable licenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are not subject to competitive bidding: (1) public safety radio services used to protect safety of life/health/property and not commercially available to the public; (2) initial licenses or construction permits for digital television service given to existing terrestrial broadcast licensees to replace analog licenses; (3) noncommercial educational and public broadcast stations described under 47 U.S.C. 397(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of competitive bidding design options
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to any competitive bidding for initial licenses, public notice shall be provided of the detailed procedures that may be used to implement auction design options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible competitive bidding design options
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish procedures for collecting bids, assigning winning bids, and determining payments, including procedures for single vs multiple rounds; bids for specific, generic, or aggregated items; bids that specify a price or indicate demand; contingent bids; staged collections; and bid modification rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assigning winning bids, procedures may take into account factors beyond the submitted bid amount, assign specific items following generic bidding, and incorporate public interest considerations. Payment-determination procedures must be consistent with other auction design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing and grouping of licenses in auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will establish the sequence in which multiple licenses will be auctioned. If using simultaneous multiple round or combinatorial bidding, the Commission will determine which licenses will be auctioned simultaneously or in combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve price policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may establish a reserve price or prices, disclosed or undisclosed, below which a license or licenses subject to auction will not be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For auctions of eligible frequencies requiring recovery of estimated relocation costs, the Commission will establish reserve prices such that total cash proceeds equal at least 110% of total estimated relocation costs provided by NTIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum/maximum bid increments and minimum opening bids
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may, by announcement before or during an auction, require minimum bid increments in dollar or percentage terms and may establish minimum opening bids and maximum bid increments on a service-specific basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping procedures for auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before or during an auction, procedures may be established regarding when bidding will stop for a round, stage, or entire auction to terminate within a reasonable time and in accordance with public interest, goals, statutory requirements, and any reserve price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may establish activity rules which require a minimum amount of bidding activity by participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal, default, and disqualification payments
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission conducts an auction pursuant to § 1.2103, it will impose payments on bidders who withdraw high bids during an auction, default on payments after an auction, or are disqualified. Withdrawal payment equals difference between withdrawn bid and winning bid in same or subsequent auction(s) (with bidding-credit considerations); interim payments (3–20%) may be assessed when final calculation is not possible. Default payment includes a deficiency payment and an additional payment (3–20% for non-combinatorial auctions; 25% for combinatorial auctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules specify calculation when intervening withdrawn bids exist, treatment of bidding credits (net vs gross), deduction of interim payments from final obligations, and examples showing numeric calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release or withholding of bidder identities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will generally release information concerning the identities of bidders before each auction but may, auction-by-auction, withhold the identity of the bidders associated with bidder identification numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to delay, suspend, or cancel auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may delay, suspend, or cancel an auction in the event of natural disaster, technical obstacle, evidence of security breach, unlawful bidding activity, administrative necessity, or any other reason affecting fair and efficient conduct of the bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may resume competitive bidding starting from current or previous round or cancel the bidding entirely at its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid apportionment and apportioned package bids
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may specify a method for apportioning a bid among portions of the license when necessary to compare bids on original or reconfigured licenses. An apportioned package bid is an estimate of the price of an individual license included in a combinatorial package and is determined by Commission methodology established in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apportioned package bids are used in place of individual bid amounts when needed to determine bidding credits, withdrawal/default obligations, tribal bidding credit limits, unjust enrichment payments, or other Commission determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form application (FCC Form 175) submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to bid, an applicant must timely submit a short-form application (FCC Form 175), together with any appropriate upfront payment set forth by Public Notice. All short-form applications must be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form applications are due on dates specified by public notice or by operation of law when mutual exclusivity is determined. The short-form must contain specified information and all statements/certifications are made under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of short-form application
rubrics_metrics.description: The short-form application must identify licenses/categories to bid on; provide applicant identification (name, corporate office/address/officer info for corporations; partners for partnerships; trustee for trusts); applicant ownership and other information per § 1.2112; identity of person(s) authorized to make/withdraw bids; designated entity certification if applicable; certifications of legal, technical, financial qualifications and foreign ownership compliance; certification of compliance with service-specific qualifications; disclosure of partnerships/joint ventures or agreements relating to licenses being auctioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes certifications that the applicant has not entered and will not enter into agreements addressing or communicating bids or bidding strategies (anti-collusion). Applicants must certify non-default/delinquent status with specified exceptions and provide certain national-security-related certifications for certain auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on collusive agreements and permitted exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification that the applicant (and parties controlling/controlled by applicant) has not and will not enter into agreements, arrangements, or understandings that address or communicate, directly or indirectly, bidding at auction (including specific prices) or bidding strategies with other applicants or certain non-applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted exceptions include agreements that are solely operational, agreements to form consortia or joint ventures, and agreements concerning transfer or assignment of licenses provided they do not both relate to the licenses at auction and address bidding/post-auction market structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls when interest in multiple short-form applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has an interest disclosed with respect to more than one short-form application for an auction, it must implement internal controls that preclude any individual acting on behalf of the applicant from possessing information about bids or bidding strategies of more than one party submitting a short-form application or communicating such information to anyone possessing such information regarding another party's short-form application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This internal control requirement applies to preventing cross-sharing of bidding strategy/bid information among related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and treatment of prior defaults/delinquencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify whether they have ever been in default on a Commission license or delinquent on non-tax debt to any Federal agency, but may exclude certain former defaults from consideration if: (A) notice received more than 7 years before short-form deadline; (B) default/delinquency was less than $100,000; (C) default/delinquency was paid within 6 months after notice of final payment deadline/delinquency; or (D) default/delinquency was cured upon resolution of legal/arbitration proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on filing short-form applications (one per entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any auction, no individual or entity may file more than one short-form application or have a controlling interest in more than one short-form application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of consortium, each member is considered to have a controlling interest in the consortium. If applications with overlapping controlling interests are filed, both will be deemed incomplete and only one may be deemed qualified. Exception applies to qualifying rural wireless partnerships meeting specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'controlling interest', de jure and de facto control, and indirect ownership calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For certifications, 'controlling interest' includes individuals/entities with positive or negative de jure or de facto control of the applicant. De jure control includes holding 50%+ of voting stock or a general partnership interest. De facto control is determined case-by-case with examples (constituting/appointing 50%+ of board; authority to appoint/promote/fire senior executives; integral role in management decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership interests held indirectly through intervening corporations may be determined by successive multiplication of ownership percentages for each link in the chain and application of relevant attribution benchmarks; if any link meets/exceeds 50% or represents actual control, it may be treated as 100% interest.
